speakers: Rob Carver (independent systematic futures trader, author)
summary: Systematic Investor 312 (Sept 2024) with Rob Carver answering listener questions on macro momentum, diversification multipliers, ATR stop losses and small accounts, then discussing a US strategic Bitcoin reserve, what ETFs really are (creation/redemption, leveraged ETP risk) and whether to just buy a CTA index (Transtrend paper; new investable SG CTA index based on a replication engine).

coverage.note: intro, Carver's current positions and low risk in drawdown
leaving the system untouched during a drawdown
detachment from news, why systematic suits most people
US unemployment/Fed view, Sept 2024 trend sector moves, three reasons to cut risk
drawdown-based risk scaling, trend index stats, macro momentum question and latent factors
asset-class momentum share of P&L, adding a lower-Sharpe strategy: use correlation
correlation rules for adding strategies, diversification multipliers (IDM/FDM)
hierarchical portfolio construction, stop-loss dual role problem start
separate position size from holding period; ATR stops and holding times
small accounts need $100k, Bitcoin strategic reserve effects
Fed balance sheet and Bitcoin flows, taxes and why Bitcoin cannot be money
US dollar advantage opinion, Bitcoin ETF holder data, gold, active ETFs intro
active ETF size, ETF as regulated wrapper, open vs closed fund structure
open-end mechanics, closed-end funds, ETF as hybrid
authorized participants, creation/redemption, ETF can hold anything
MicroStrategy 3x ETP, ETF due diligence, new CTA index introduced
Transtrend paper: stock index vs CTA index as factor exposure, pick winners vs index
CTA manager diversification, limits of stock-index analogy
more markets, nonlinearity, SG CTA index breadth, purposes of an index
ETFs for retail, bottom-up replication, fewer than 20 markets cannot deliver index
back-test as public track record risk
bottom line: understand what is inside any ETF; outro

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I'm currently long equities long bonds um and short um some sort of gas and agricultural markets
claims.claim: Sept 2024 snapshot of Carver's trend system after a poor few months: long equities and bonds (a risk-parity-like stance) and short gas and agricultural markets.
claims.direction: long equities and bonds, short gas and ags

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: running quite low risk at the moment is what we'd expect in the middle of a draw down
claims.claim: In a drawdown models find weak forecasts and many markets have low volatility, so a volatility-targeted trend system runs low risk.
claims.testable: yes - risk level vs drawdown can be tested

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the big Temptation when you're losing money is to change your system and change your strategy and Fiddle with things
claims.claim: Leaving the system alone is easier when away; the main temptation in a drawdown is to fiddle with the system.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: systematic trading suits me and probably most people out there um better than than discretionary
claims.claim: Systematic trading suits most people because detached emotion is very hard for discretionary traders.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I wouldn't be surprised if they just do 25 basis points at each of the next three meetings
claims.claim: Sept 2024 view: US unemployment data (due that day) would set the Fed path; soft data since April; he expected 25bp cuts at each of the three remaining meetings.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: equities uh are down in price but they're also hurting Trend followers
claims.claim: First week of Sept 2024: falling equities hurt long-biased trend followers while rising bonds helped, and a grain correction hurt short positions.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: August may have been the month that tricked a lot of risk reduction overall in CTA portfolios
claims.claim: Direction flips in major sectors in August 2024 changed correlations and triggered broad risk reduction in CTA portfolios.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: you basically reduce risk for two reasons one one reason being that you you know the trends turn against you
claims.claim: A trend system reduces risk for three reasons: trends turn against you (continuous forecast or stop loss), volatility rises (for vol-targeted systems), and you are losing money.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: if you lose 10% of your of you know of your account value then you should reduce your positions by 10% even if nothing else has changed
claims.claim: Scale positions with account value: after a 10% loss cut positions by 10% (open or closed trade equity).
claims.direction: reduce positions proportionally to equity loss
claims.testable: yes - equity-based risk scaling is backtestable

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it finished at 50 yesterday so that's actually a pretty good number
claims.claim: Trend barometer 50 on 5 Sept 2024 with SG indices up about 1-2.5% YTD; MSCI World +12.6%, S&P 500 +15.4%.
claims.indicator: Trend barometer, SG CTA/Trend/Short-term Traders indices

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the there's a bunch of latent factors in the world that you can't see and when we do momentum all we're doing really is is doing momentum on individual markets
claims.claim: Theory behind macro momentum: unobservable latent factors form trends and momentum on individual markets is a window onto them; AQR proposes trending macro factors directly.
claims.indicator: latent factors; AQR A Half Century of Macro Momentum
claims.testable: partly - macro vs price momentum can be tested

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: that actually captures about 80 to 85% of the p&l of trading the individual markets
claims.claim: Evidence for latent factors: asset-class-level momentum (synthetic index per asset class) captures about 80-85% of the P&L of trading individual markets, the remainder being relative momentum.
claims.indicator: asset-class momentum vs individual market momentum

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: my suspicion is that macr momentum is quite correlated with um price trend
claims.claim: Macro momentum is probably quite correlated with price trend because both rest on the same latent factors, so adding it probably improves Sharpe only modestly.
claims.indicator: macro momentum vs price trend correlation

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: something that has a lower Shar ratio but has got a lot of very low correl or even negative correlation
claims.claim: Portfolio Sharpe rises by adding either a higher-Sharpe stream or a lower-Sharpe stream with very low or negative correlation; a fall from 1.3 to 1.2 is not a deal-breaker.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: sharp ratios are a lot more variable and harder to forecast
claims.claim: When adding strategies look at correlation rather than Sharpe, because Sharpe ratios are noisier and more dispersed in backtests than correlations.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: probably think that's worth adding 5 10% to this even if it does reduce the back tested sh ratio
claims.claim: If correlation to existing strategy is around 0.4, allocate 5-10% even if the backtested Sharpe falls, trusting diversification more than Sharpe.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: if on the other hand the correlation is like 8.9 between say macro momentum and price momentum
claims.claim: If correlation is about 0.89 the extra work is not worth it for an individual, although a big fund with staff may still benefit.
claims.conditions: for an individual with limited resources

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I'll find that my volatility drops from 25% to about 8%
claims.claim: Instrument and forecast diversification multipliers (IDM/FDM) rescale combined streams back to the target standard deviation: with 150-200 markets portfolio volatility falls from 25% to about 8% without them.
claims.direction: scale up positions to target vol

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I do my portfolio Construction in a hierarchical way
claims.claim: Hierarchical construction: instead of extra multipliers at each level, give higher risk weight to groups with more internal diversification (e.g. more momentum signals than carry signals).

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: is faecally doing two jobs for you
claims.claim: A stop loss both sets risk per trade and the holding period, creating a false choice between large risk with long holding and tight risk with premature exits.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: want to do is completely separate out these two decisions so one decision is how big should my positions be and the second decision is how long should I hold my positions for
claims.claim: Separate position size (risk) from holding period (speed of trading) instead of tying both to stops.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I think 4 atrs would give you a holding period of about a month
claims.claim: A 4 ATR stop gives about a month's holding, typical CTA futures; 8 ATR gives about three months; much tighter makes you a short-term trend trader.
claims.indicator: ATR stop width vs holding period

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: you do take more risk per trade but because you're taking fewer trades your actual overall risk stays the same
claims.claim: A wider ATR stop means more risk per trade but fewer trades, so overall risk is similar or lower than a tight stop with 2% per trade, which trades often and has bigger volatility and drawdowns.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: you probably should be looking at least $100,000 to trade a diversified portfolio Futures
claims.claim: Below roughly $100,000 even micros and minis give a portfolio dominated by equity indices and agriculturals; smaller investors are better off with a CTA ETF or fund.
claims.direction: use CTA ETF until account grows

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: be quietly High correlated to Trump's chances of winning
claims.claim: Sept 2024: floating a US strategic Bitcoin reserve (US buying lifts price) makes Bitcoin a proxy for Trump's election chances.
claims.testable: partly - correlation with polls could be tested

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I think most people agree now it's just a purely speculative asset
claims.claim: Bitcoin has lost its original claim as money and is viewed as a speculative asset.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: it's not going to change the fed's balance sheet very much but it may potentially change bitcoin's price quite a lot because it would be quite a big flow of money
claims.claim: A small central bank Bitcoin allocation would barely change a balance sheet but would move Bitcoin's price through the size of the flow.
claims.conditions: if a strategic reserve is created

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: there's no way any government would be crazy enough to say oh yeah well you can pay your taxes in this other thing that we don't control
claims.claim: Currencies derive value from tax acceptance and government creation; governments will not accept an asset they do not control for taxes, so Bitcoin cannot be money.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: most institutional investors who allocate in q1 either held or bought more shares this spring
claims.claim: Despite Trump odds, Bitcoin and ether fell (ether -22% in August) and gold made new highs, though 54% of institutional filers raised Bitcoin ETF positions in Q2.
claims.indicator: 13F Bitcoin ETF holdings, Bitcoin, ether, gold

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the actively managed ETFs have now hit apparently a trillion dollars
claims.claim: Active ETFs reached $1tn but only about 10-15% of the ETF universe, which is still mostly passive.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: there are a huge number of Institutions that cannot legally buy crypto outright or do not want to buy crypto outright
claims.claim: The ETF wrapper acts as a regulatory stamp that lets institutions that cannot hold crypto or futures buy exposure, widening demand.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: take advantage of that with creation Redemption and that keeps the price honest
claims.claim: Authorized participants create and redeem ETF shares in kind, so price stays close to NAV, unlike closed-end funds that can trade at large discounts or premiums.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: because you can literally put anything into this thing anything
claims.claim: The ETF is just a legal wrapper, not a safety label; it can hold single shares triple-leveraged.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: while micro strategy itself is higher by more than 100% this year LMI 3 has dropped nearly 82%
claims.claim: A 3x leveraged daily ETP on MicroStrategy (LMI3) lost about 82% while MicroStrategy rose over 100%, showing the compounding damage of leveraged ETFs.
claims.conditions: leveraged daily ETFs in volatile assets

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: with ETFs people don't do I I think don't do much due diligence
claims.claim: ETF buyers do little due diligence compared with hedge fund allocators.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: by buying a stock index what you're actually buying is effectively One Step removed a exposure to a whole bunch of factors
claims.claim: Transtrend paper argument: a stock index is indirect exposure to factors such as yen and metals, and a CTA index is likewise exposure to factors via many CTAs.
claims.indicator: Transtrend 'Can't we just buy the index'

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: if you think you're good at picking winners if you think you can pick good ctas either based on their past performance or based on due diligence then you should probably do that rather than buy an index
claims.claim: If you can pick winning CTAs, do so rather than index; the index is for those who cannot.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: because CT managers are quite correlated you don't need that many of them to give you a kind of reasonable divers
claims.claim: With 30-50 million, pick around 10 CTA managers since they are correlated.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: most companies do hedge out their exposure to their principal risk
claims.claim: Weakness in the stock-index analogy: firms hedge FX and commodity exposures.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: CTS change their exposure dynamically sometimes they're long sometimes they're short
claims.claim: CTA factor exposure is dynamic and not linear or one-directional, unlike a company's.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: in the much more in the more is better Camp
claims.claim: More markets are better than fewer, so replicating with a small number of futures is not ideal.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: correlations to poor poor judge of of anything that isn't linear
claims.claim: High correlation between CTAs does not prevent outliers; picking your own CTAs can miss an exploding manager, like missing Nvidia in a picked stock portfolio.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: even 20 is not a big number for an index
claims.claim: The SG CTA index has only 20 managers, so it can be undiversified if it misses a big winner.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I'm going to use this index for 20 years of history as a proxy for the CTA universe
claims.claim: An index serves for benchmarking and as long-history proxy in asset allocation, which is institutional thinking.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I'm more of a fan of doing bottomup replication the top down
claims.claim: Prefers bottom-up replication (replicate positions) over top-down (replicate an index) for statistical reasons.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: every day I try and replicate that big portfolio with my smaller portfolio
claims.claim: Carver's own implementation generates positions in about 250 futures (60 untradeable) and replicates them in a small account.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: how can an ETF that trades in fewer than 20 markets deliver CTA index Returns the answer is simple it cannot
claims.claim: An ETF with fewer than 20 markets may be correlated with the CTA index but lacks its diversification and carries single-manager risk (Transtrend).

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: ETFs are a good thing for retail investors
claims.claim: ETFs give retail access to alternative risk premia and trend following that would otherwise be unavailable.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: however now that it's labeled an index and people think okay well I can now go and buy that index a back test becomes quote unquote a public track record
claims.claim: Labelling a backtest as an index makes it a public track record, which could mislead since managers cannot sell on backtests.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: as with any ETF product don't just buy it and think it's safe because it says ETF on the outside
claims.claim: Understand what is inside any ETF; the new investable CTA index is more trustworthy than a triple-leveraged Bitcoin ETP.
